text.p: Steelmaker Hylsamex's board of directors have approved total investments of $210 million in production processes over the coming 18 months, which it plans to finance from in-house funds and bank loans, the company's press officer said on Wednesday.

At a meeting on Tuesday, the Hylsamex board approved spending of $137 million on expanding its minimill, and $73 million to increase production of higher value-added products, such as galvanized and cold-rolled sheet.
"We plan to obtain the ($210 million) financing from a combination of in-house resources and loans from foreign trade banks," Hylsamex press officer Humberto Estrella said in a telephone interview.
Estrella confirmed earlier reports that Hylsamex also planned to raise $100 million in a stock placement.
"If it is deemed convenient, Hylsamex will look into a placement on the international capital markets," he added.
